paragraphs: One-sentence judgment: biologists are not a job for people who simply like plants and animals, but a scientist position centered on research questions and sampling or experimental design and data interpretation and conclusions: the official responsibility is to study the basic principles of plant and animal life (origin and relationships and development and anatomy and function), and common work includes identifying and classifying and studying the structure and behavior and ecology and physiology and nutrition and culture and distribution of species, collecting and analyzing data on the relationships between organisms and their environment, studying aquatic plants and animals and the environmental conditions affected by radiation or pollution, studying and managing wildlife populations, measuring physical conditions such as water salinity and acidity and light and oxygen content and judging their relationship to aquatic organisms, drafting renewable resource management plans, developing pest management and control measures and carrying out pest exclusion risk assessments, developing methods and devices for obtaining representative plant and animal and aquatic or soil samples, assessing the environmental impact of present and potential uses of land and water bodies, writing technical and research reports (such as environmental impact statements), communicating results to industry and government and the public, writing grant proposals to apply for research funding, teaching or advising students and conducting research at colleges and universities, supervising biological technicians and technologists and other scientists, representing the employer at conferences in a technical capacity, and planning and managing biological research projects for government or research institutions or the pharmaceutical industry or manufacturing; people who want definite answers and are unwilling to bear the uncertainty of sampling and experiments, unwilling to write methods and limitations and uncertainty clearly, and unwilling to stop at authorization and biosecurity and ethics boundaries are not suited to it.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to trace a research question back to the sampling design or experimental conditions and the raw data; you can travel back and forth among the field and the laboratory and data analysis over long periods and keep the records reproducible; when results do not match expectations or sample representativeness is insufficient or instruments are anomalous you are willing to review first and record truthfully rather than picking the data that are usable; you are willing to stop first and follow the approval and reporting process when restricted species and ecological locations and human genetic resources and pathogenic microorganisms are involved or your authorization is exceeded.

Conditions for pausing your investment first: you have not yet completed, under any supervised condition, one full closed loop of confirming the question and hypothesis, sampling or experimental design, data collection and recording, analysis methods and limitations review, and stating conclusions and uncertainty, or you can only explain your interest by liking animals or liking to watch documentaries; nor should you treat having taken a biology course or being able to use one analysis software as proof that you can independently decide the research plan or independently publish research conclusions and handle restricted species and pathogenic microorganisms and genetic resource data. Field work and sampling and pathogenic microorganisms and restricted species and human genetic resources must be handled in accordance with the applicable jurisdiction and competent authorities and institutional systems and records must be retained; this page does not provide any practice for circumventing regulation.

One sentence: this is a scientist position centered on research questions and data interpretation and conclusions that works under sampling and experimental design and biosecurity and ecological and genetic resource rules; the core is writing the question and hypothesis and sampling or experimental design and data and limitations clearly and accepting peer review, not a romantic imagination of nature; its U.S. wage and employment and projection data are given on the O*NET page in the parent occupation 19-1029.00 scope with labels at every occurrence, and the industry distribution is in the 19-1029.04 scope for this occupation; on the mainland China side no nationally comparable wage scope corresponding one-to-one to this occupation was obtained, and this page publishes no mainland China wage figures and visibly marks the gap as insufficient evidence.

The work of biologists can be divided into three categories: research tasks (identify and classify and study the structure and behavior and ecology and physiology and nutrition and culture and distribution of species; study the basic principles of plant and animal life; collect and analyze data on the relationships between organisms and their environment; study aquatic plants and animals and how they are affected by environmental conditions; study and manage wildlife populations; measure physical conditions such as water salinity and acidity and light and oxygen content; study the responses of plants and animals and marine species to parasites; carry out process research on natural and industrial ecosystems); data and results and compliance (use computers to store and process and analyze data; write technical and research reports and communicate results to industry and government and the public; review the accuracy and sufficiency and compliance of reports and proposals such as land use classification and recreational development; write grant proposals; assess the environmental impact of land use and water bodies and propose improvement methods; develop pest management and control measures and carry out risk assessment; develop methods and devices for obtaining representative plant and animal and aquatic or soil samples); and collaboration and training and project organization (establish and maintain liaisons and effective working relationships with groups and individuals and institutions and the public; supervise biological technicians and technologists and other scientists; teach or advise students and conduct research at colleges and universities; represent the employer at conferences in a technical capacity; prepare requests for proposals or statements of work; plan and manage biological research projects for government or research institutions or the pharmaceutical industry or manufacturing; take inventory of and order laboratory supplies). What the three categories share is writing the research question and sampling or experimental conditions and methods and limitations clearly, rather than taking the desired results first and adding the conditions afterwards.

The basis for comparison is the official occupation description of O*NET 19-1029.04 and the list of related occupations on the O*NET page (Biochemists and Biophysicists, Biological Technicians, Conservation Scientists, Geneticists, Geoscientists, Except Hydrologists and Geographers, Microbiologists, Molecular and Cellular Biologists, Natural Sciences Managers, Soil and Plant Scientists, Zoologists and Wildlife Biologists, Bioinformatics Scientists, Industrial Ecologists, Environmental Science Teachers, Postsecondary, Environmental Scientists and Specialists, Including Health, Medical Scientists, Except Epidemiologists, Biological Science Teachers, Postsecondary, Forestry and Conservation Science Teachers, Postsecondary, Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers, Environmental Restoration Planners, Medical and Clinical Laboratory Technologists and others), as well as the adjacent occupation relationships noted in the routing materials; an adjacent relationship only indicates proximity of duties and does not mean that qualifications, authorization or positions are interchangeable.

The table below compares biologists with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: occupational direction, core work and outputs, key differences, and which choice suits each preference.

Bioinformatics scientists take computational strategy and statistical inference as their main object and decide the analysis path at the data and method level; biologists take research questions and sampling or experimental design and data interpretation as their main object and need to handle real field and environmental and biological material conditions.

If you would rather define computational methods and statistical inference, compare bioinformatics scientists first; if you would rather do sampling and experiments and data interpretation, then this occupation suits you.
Complete computational methods and statistical inference, with outputs mainly in analysis workflows and methods and papers.
Biologists and bioinformatics scientists

Biological technicians take completing experimental preparation and data collection and observation according to established plans as their main object and do not take on research design and conclusion determination; biologists take question and hypothesis setting and method selection and conclusion interpretation as their main object.

If you would rather make established plans stable and accurate and record truthfully, compare biological technicians first; if you would rather define questions and interpret conclusions, then this occupation suits you.
Complete experimental preparation and data collection according to standard operating procedures, with outputs mainly in experimental records and datasets.
Biologists and biological technicians

Microbiologists take microorganisms and culture and identification and biosecurity as their main object; biologists take the principles of plant and animal life and species and ecology and distribution as their main object and need to consider field and environmental conditions at the same time.

If you would rather do microorganisms and culture and identification, compare microbiologists first; if you would rather do species and ecology and environmental condition research, then this occupation suits you.
Complete microorganism culture and identification and related experiments, with outputs mainly in strains and testing and experimental results.
Biologists and microbiologists

Molecular and cellular biologists take mechanisms at the cellular and molecular level as their main object and mostly work in controlled experimental systems; biologists take species and ecology and environment and distribution as their main object and need to handle sampling representativeness and uncontrollable field conditions.

If you would rather do mechanism research in controlled systems, compare molecular and cellular biologists first; if you would rather do species and ecology and environment research, then this occupation suits you.
Complete cellular and molecular experiments and mechanism interpretation, with outputs mainly in experimental data and mechanism papers.
Biologists and molecular and cellular biologists

Soil and plant scientists take soil and crops and plant production systems as their main object and lean toward agriculture and production system applications; biologists take the principles of plant and animal life in natural and environmental settings as their main object.

If you would rather do soil and crops and production systems, compare soil and plant scientists first; if you would rather do species and ecology research in natural settings, then this occupation suits you.
Complete surveys and trials of soil and crops and production systems, with outputs mainly in production recommendations and trial data.
Biologists and soil and plant scientists

Conservation scientists take resource conservation and land and water management as their main object and lean toward the implementation of management policy and conservation measures; biologists take the study of life principles and species and ecological processes as their main object.

If you would rather do the implementation of conservation measures and management plans, compare conservation scientists first; if you would rather do basic and ecological research, then this occupation suits you.

entries.answer: Research the basic principles of plant and animal life (origin, relationships, development, anatomy, and function). Common tasks include identifying, classifying, and studying the structure, behavior, ecology, physiology, nutrition, culture, and distribution of species; collecting and analyzing data on organisms and their environmental relationships; studying aquatic plants and animals and the environmental conditions affected by radioactivity or pollution; studying and managing wildlife populations; measuring physical conditions such as water salinity, acidity, light, and oxygen content and determining their relationship to aquatic life; drafting renewable resource management plans; developing pest management and control measures and conducting pest exclusion risk assessments; developing methods and devices for obtaining representative plant, animal, and aquatic or soil samples; assessing the environmental impact of present and potential uses of land and water; writing technical and research reports and communicating results to industry, government, and the public; writing grant proposals to apply for research funding; teaching or advising students and conducting research at colleges and universities; supervising biological technicians and technologists and other scientists; representing the employer at meetings in a technical capacity; and planning and managing biological research projects for government, research institutions, the pharmaceutical industry, or manufacturing.

entries.answer: Key risks include exceeding sampling permits and research authorizations; compliance risks around restricted species, ecological locations, and genetic resource data; raw data, methods, and samples that cannot be reproduced; automated analysis and model output being treated as conclusions; field and laboratory exposure and workload; and exceeding boundaries when reporting or transferring results, data, and samples. Controls are to work first within the authorized sampling, experiment, and ethics scope and identify risks; handle restricted species, genetic resources, pathogenic microorganisms, and animals according to procedure and keep records; honestly record the sampling design, samples, methods, versions, data, and anomalies; hand over results and provide data and samples only within the authorized scope; and stop and escalate when you exceed authorization or find anomalies.

entries.answer: Look at reviewable outputs: whether you can pose questions and hypotheses and collect and analyze data according to a plan, whether you can honestly record methods, environment, and anomalies and keep things reproducible, and whether you can stop, review, and report when results do not match expectations, sample representativeness is insufficient, data are anomalous, or you exceed authorization. hero.quick_answer: Biologists research the basic principles of plant and animal life, and the official duty statement is Research or study basic principles of plant and animal life, such as origin, relationship, development, anatomy, and functions; common tasks include identifying, classifying, and studying the structure, behavior, ecology, physiology, nutrition, culture, and distribution of species, collecting and analyzing data on organisms and their environmental relationships, studying aquatic plants and animals and the environmental conditions affected by radioactivity or pollution, studying and managing wildlife populations, measuring physical conditions such as water salinity, acidity, light, and oxygen content, drafting renewable resource management plans, developing pest management and control measures and conducting risk assessments, developing methods and devices for obtaining representative plant, animal, and aquatic or soil samples, assessing the environmental impact of present and potential uses of land and water, writing technical and research reports and communicating results to industry, government, and the public, writing grant proposals to apply for research funding, teaching or advising students and conducting research at colleges and universities, supervising biological technicians and technologists and other scientists, representing the employer at meetings in a technical capacity, and planning and managing biological research projects for government, research institutions, the pharmaceutical industry, or manufacturing; the work is not the same as the final determination of research conclusions or the approval of restricted species sampling or providing human genetic resources externally, and does not replace the regulatory requirements of the applicable jurisdiction, competent departments, and institutional rules for biosafety, ecological protection, genetic resource management, and animal welfare, and you should stop and escalate when sampling permits are non-compliant, when restricted or endangered species, human genetic resources, high-grade pathogenic microorganisms, or animal experiments and other situations requiring special approval are involved, or when data anomalies, method failures, or work beyond your authorization are found.

description.text: What biologists do, what education and preparation is needed, what income and prospects look like in the United States, which tasks AI will change, and the boundaries of exceeding sampling permits and research authorizations, compliance risks around restricted species and ecological locations and genetic resource data, raw data and methods and samples that cannot be reproduced, automated analysis and model output being treated as conclusions, field and laboratory exposure and workload, and reporting and transferring results, data, and samples externally; definitions, source scope, and data gaps are retained.

subject.name: Biologists
subject.summary: Biologists study the basic principles of plant and animal life (origin and relationships and development and anatomy and function), and common work includes identifying and classifying and studying the structure and behavior and ecology and physiology and nutrition and culture and distribution of species, collecting and analyzing data on the relationships between organisms and their environment, studying and managing wildlife populations, measuring physical conditions such as water salinity and acidity and light and oxygen content, assessing the environmental impact of land use and water bodies, developing pest management and control measures, developing methods and devices for obtaining representative samples, writing technical and research reports and grant proposals, teaching or advising students and conducting research at colleges and universities, supervising biological technicians and technologists and other scientists, and planning and managing biological research projects for government or research institutions or the pharmaceutical industry or manufacturing. The U.S. side corresponds to O*NET 19-1029.04 (Biologists), which is Job Zone Five (extensive preparation needed); the identity and tasks and work context and skills for this occupation are in the 19-1029.04 scope for this occupation; the wage and employment and projection are explicitly labeled on the O*NET page as taken from the parent occupation Biological Scientists, All Other (19-1029.00), and this page publishes according to the page values with the parent occupation scope and data period labeled at every occurrence; the industry distribution is in the 19-1029.04 scope for this occupation. On the mainland China side no occupational wage entry precisely corresponding to this occupation was obtained, so according to the evidence standard this page publishes no mainland China wage figures and retains a visible gap marker, without passing off industry averages as an occupational median; field sampling and genetic resources and biosecurity in mainland China are subject to the Biosecurity Law of the People's Republic of China and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Administration of Human Genetic Resources and other provisions.
